intro_html: One sheet pan, no searing, no breading, no fuss. The chops and the potatoes go into the same oven under a sweet and tangy pantry glaze built from ketchup, brown sugar, soy sauce and cider vinegar. It comes out at 44 grams of protein for about $3.62 (at everyday cost), which is the kind of math that makes a Sunday afternoon feel productive.
cost_closing_html: About $3.62 a bowl (at everyday cost) for a full pork chop dinner with the potatoes already on the plate. That is a restaurant entree price cut down to pocket change.
shop_smart: The chops are the whole budget here. Everything else in this recipe combined costs less than a third of the meat. Watch the board for a pork chop sale and buy the family pack when it hits.
The glaze is all pantry. Ketchup, soy sauce, brown sugar, Worcestershire and cider vinegar cost almost nothing per batch and every one of those bottles lives in your cabinet for months.
Buy potatoes by the seven pound bag. Loose potatoes cost roughly double per pound and this recipe eats a lot of them.
One head of garlic covers this batch twice over. Skip the jarred stuff. Fresh cloves are cheaper and taste like something.
make_it: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Heat the oven to 400F and line two large sheet pans.
Whisk the Worcestershire, ketchup, soy sauce, brown sugar, olive oil, minced garlic and apple cider vinegar together into a glossy glaze.
Cut the potatoes into even wedges, toss them with about a third of the glaze plus salt and pepper, and spread them in a single layer on the pans.
Roast the potatoes alone first so they get a head start and start to brown at the edges.
Season the pork chops, nestle them among the potatoes, and brush them generously with the remaining glaze.
Return the pans to the oven and bake until the chops hit 145F inside and the glaze has gone sticky.
Rest the chops five minutes, then slice them off the bone and combine everything in your big pot with the pan juices.
portion_html: Set the full pot on your scale and subtract the empty pot weight from Step 1. Divide that total by 14 and scoop the exact amount into each container so the meat and potatoes land even across the board. Every bowl comes in near 561 calories with a serious 44 grams of protein.

head.description: Sheet pan pork chops and potatoes under a sweet tangy pantry glaze, built for 14 servings. 561 calories, 44g protein, about $3.62 per serving (at everyday cost).
head.keywords: oven baked pork chops, sheet pan pork chops and potatoes, country style pork chops, budget pork meal prep, easy pork dinner
steps: Whisk the ketchup, brown sugar, soy sauce, Worcestershire, cider vinegar, olive oil and garlic into a glaze.
Toss the potato wedges with part of the glaze and roast them on lined sheet pans until they start to brown.
Add the seasoned pork chops to the pans and brush with the remaining glaze.
Bake until the chops reach 145F inside and the glaze turns sticky.
Rest, slice, and combine with the potatoes and pan juices.
